meta.scenario: tech house energy-sustain blend — T1 has chopped vocal hook in outro; eq(T1, mid=0.4) timed to cut hook before T2 groove arrives; eq restore on T1 not needed (T1 fading out)

transition_arc: T1 has a chopped vocal hook ('I'm losing it') that recurs every 4 bars through the outro (bars 64–80). The hook is mid-range-heavy (200–3000 Hz choppy fragment) and would compete with T2's incoming groove during the blend — not a full vocal clash but a mid-range interference problem. The solution: eq(T1, mid=0.4) fires 4 bars into the blend window (not at the start) so the audience has a brief moment of T1's hook playing alongside T2's incoming percussion, then it fades under the mid cut. This feels more musical than cutting it immediately. T2 is a clean instrumental tech house track — no competing vocal, so the mid suppression is moderate (0.4, not 0.2). EQ restore is NOT needed on T1 because T1 is fading out — the EQ change on an outgoing track is harmless.

annotated_actions.t1_state: T1 bar 0: full peak tech house, 'Losing It' vocal hook active, RMS 0.65
T1 bar 56: 8 bars before T2 fade_in at bar 64. Groove at full energy, chopped vocal hook cycling
annotated_actions.why: Bass pre-cut 8 bars before T2 enters. Mid left at 1.0 here — the chopped hook continues at full impact for these 8 bars. The audience still hears the iconic hook as T1's outro runs, which is desirable (don't suppress it prematurely).
Kill T2 bass at fade start — prevents dual basslines during blend. EQ is persistent; will be restored at bass_swap point.

annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 bar 8: clean instrumental intro, kick+hats active, harmonic=0.08, drums=0.40
annotated_actions.why: Standard fade_in. T2 is purely instrumental — no competing vocal. other:0.5 for Camelot +1 compatibility. from_bar=8 skips T2's 8 near-silent opening bars. stems={drums:0.8, bass:0.0, other:0.6} — T2 enters with 80% drums, no bass (held for bass_swap), 60% atmosphere.

annotated_actions.t1_state: T1 bar 68: 4 bars into T2 fade_in. Chopped hook cycling, T2 drums now audible alongside
annotated_actions.why: Mid suppression fires 4 bars AFTER T2's fade_in starts (bar 64 + 4 = bar 68) — not simultaneously. This is intentional: the audience hears one last cycle of the T1 hook alongside T2's incoming percussion (bars 64–68), then the hook fades under the mid cut. This is more musical than suppressing immediately — the hook gets a 'last moment' before it dissolves. mid=0.4 (≈−4 dB) is moderate: the hook becomes a muffled background texture, not completely cut. Restoration NOT required on T1 because T1 is fading out (fade_out active) — EQ changes on an outgoing track don't persist into the rest of the mix.

annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 bar 16 (from_bar=8, 8 bars elapsed): bass entering, groove locking in
annotated_actions.why: Midpoint of the 16-bar window (64 + 8 = 72). Swap releases T2's bass stem.
Restore T2 bass at bass_swap point — T1 bass is now HPF-cut, T2 bass can come in.
Simultaneous with T2 fade_in. 16-bar fade_out. The mid-suppressed vocal hook fades gracefully.
